chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muhammad ibn Hakim, who said:

I said to Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him): 'Do the major sins (al-kaba'ir) take one out of faith (iman)?' He said: 'Yes.' And what is besides the major sins? The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The adulterer does not commit adultery while he is a believer, and the thief does not steal while he is a believer.'
ai.seo_question: Do major sins take a Muslim out of the fold of faith (Iman)?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi elucidates the Shia doctrine of 'Baqaa al-Iman' (the permanence of faith), affirming that major sins do not nullify one's status as a believer but rather diminish the perfection of their faith. It aligns with the Ahl al-Bayt's view against the Khawarij, who held that major sins constitute disbelief (kufr), by citing the Prophet's statement that the adulterer and thief remain believers despite their transgressions. This highlights the distinction between the ontological state of iman and its practical manifestation in action.
